tossups.text: This author wrote a poem that notes how the title group "makes me sick, they make me tired" after writing how "they hail you as the morning star." This poet wrote, "Count to ten, and man is bored" in a poem that opens "Women wants monogamy; Man delights in novelty." This author of "General Review of the Sex Situation" opened a poem with the lines "My own dear love, he is strong and bold / And he cares not what comes after." That poem, which ends "I wish somebody'd shoot him," is titled "Love Song." An eight-line poem by this author notes "Acids stain you" and "Gas smells awful" in a poem that opens "Razors pain you." The line "You might as well live" closes this author's poem "Resume." This author cynically wrote, "Men seldom make passes / At girls who wear glasses." For 10 points, name this witty member of the Algonquin Round Table.

For her role in this event, boarding house owner Mary Surratt became the first woman executed by the U.S. federal government. Dr. Samuel Mudd treated this event's perpetrator for a broken leg he got while jumping on to the stage of Ford's Theatre during a performance of Our American Cousin. The words "Sic semper tyrannis" were shouted by the perpetrator of, for 10 points, what event that saw John Wilkes Booth kill the 16th President?

In human physiology, this structure is essential for atp and muscle energy. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this contraction-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The contraction is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in atp and muscle energy.

tossups.text: Jan Tinbergen ["yahn TIN-bairg-in"] and Ragnar Frisch applied statistical methods to this discipline to develop a subfield named for a portmanteau of this discipline and "metrics." Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman applied psychology to decision-making in this discipline's "behavioral" subfield. This discipline is divided into small scale "micro" and large scale "macro" types. For 10 points, name this study of production and consumption of goods and services.

The Flongle is a device that performs this task by measuring disruptions of an ionic current. One method to perform this task requires tagmentation to be completed beforehand. The Min·ION is another device for performing this task created by a company named for Oxford. If shotgunning is used to complete this task, contigs must be combined for assembly. Bridge amplification is used in the method for performing this task that was invented by Illumina, in which certain molecules bind to oligos on aflow cell. That device uses a tether to guide a certain molecule into a nanopore, allowing this task to be performed with long reads. One method to perform this task uses d·d·N·T·Ps to achieve chain termination and is named for Frederick Sanger. For 10 points, what task was performed on an entire genome by the Human Genome Project?

A model first developed to describe this phenomenon predicts that the fraction of low energy states equals the negative hyperbolic tangent of beta times the splitting energy. This phenomenon only occurs if the density of states at the Fermi level times the Stoner exchange parameter is greater than one. Heisenberg modified a model of this phenomenon that simply defines points in a lattice to be spin-up or spin-down. A graph of this phenomenon has intercepts labelled coercivity and remanence and forms a hysteresis loop with steps for gaussing and degaussing. Below the Curie temperature, this phenomenon occurs when domains align in the absence of an external field. For 10 points, name this form of permanent magnetism observed in cobalt, nickel, and iron.

This man used an ant to thread a string through a conch shell for the King of Crete. A structure created by this man imprisoned the son of Pasiphae and a white bull, and was navigated by Theseus using a ball of string. This man used honey and wax to build wings after he and his son were imprisoned by Minos for building the Labyrinth. For 10 points, name this Greek inventor, whose son Icarus died after flying too close to the sun.

Vincenzo Peruggia attempted to return this painting to Florence, where this painting's sfumato background of a winding road and an arched bridge were painted. This wood-panel painting is nicknamed "La Joconde" at its home in the Louvre, and likely shows the wife of Francesco del Giocondo wearing a veil and lacking any visible lashes or eyebrows. For 10 points, name this painting by Leonardo da Vinci of a seated woman with an enigmatic smile.

A monocle-wearing character in this novella is said to be able to "turn black into white" to justify taking additional milk and apples. A character in this book is visited multiple times a day as his progress in designing a windmill is tracked. Characters in this novella are taught the song "Beasts of England" by Old Major. A maxim in this novella is changed to refer to some members of a group being "more equal than others." Napoleon murders his fellow revolutionary pig Snowball in, for 10 points, what novella by George Orwell?

In one story by these authors, an aged donkey recruits a dog, a cat, and a rooster to sing with him and scare away some burglars. In another, two children mark their path home with bread crumbs. These men wrote about a girl who lives with seven dwarfs, and another whose foot fits a gold slipper. For 10 points, name these German brothers, the authors of "The Bremen Town Musicians," "Hansel and Gretel," "Snow White," and "Cinderella."

This man created a work that was criticized by some to be sculpted from a living model. Another of this man's works was left unfinished and contains segments such as The Old Courtesan and The Three Shades, who point to the words "Abandon all hope, ye who enter here." This sculptor of The Bronze Age and The Gates of Hell also created a large bronze sculpture of six martyrs of the Hundred Years' War and one based off of Dante. For 10 points, identify this French sculptor of The Burghers of Calais and The Thinker.

His pseudonym meant "Doctor Hopeful." Born in Bialystok, Poland, this physician's most famous accomplishment was first chronicled in the 1887 book Lingvo Internacia. For ten points, name this Pole who developed the artificial language now known as Esperanto.

Three bodyguards of a 2014 presidential candidate in this country were killed by a suicide bomber in an assassination attempt. A tunnel complex in this country's Khorasan region was the target for the first use of the MOAB bomb, the largest non-nuclear bomb. Operation Resolute Support is ongoing in this country where Ashraf Ghani defeated Abdullah Abdullah to succeed Hamid Karzai as president. President Trump promised to send 3,000 more troops to, for 10 points, what country once led by the Taliban from Kabul?

The dimethyl of this element is a particularly potent toxin that can penetrate nitrile gloves. The vaccine preservative thimerosal has been banned in some countries for containing this element, which forms amalgams with other metals. A common unit of pressure is millimeters of this element, once used in thermometers since it is a liquid at room temperature. For 10 points, name this element with symbol Hg that shares its name with the planet closest to the Sun.

This city, home to the War Memorial Opera House, has such suburbs as Daly City. In it can be found Russian Hill and Lake Merced as well as Nob Hill. This city's district of Haight-Ashbury was a center of hippie culture. Its namesake body of water contains Treasure Island and Angel Island; across that bay lies Oakland. For 10 points, name this city at the south end of the Golden Gate Bridge.

One religious movement in this modern-day country began in a printer's house during Lent when two sausages were cut up and eaten. The burning of anti-Trinitarian Michael Servetus occurred in this country, where religious tension fueled the Kappel wars. A reformer from here argued for a purely symbolic Eucharist at the Marburg Colloquy. The first society based around the book Institutes of the Christian Religion was here; that society's founder believed in an elect that God chose by predestination. For 10 points, name this country split into cantons, the home country of Ulrich Zwingli, where John Calvin ran a theocracy in Geneva.
acceptableAnswers: either underlined part of Schweizerische Eidgenossenschaft

tossups.text: In the music video of one song with this title, Novak Djokovic ("JOE-koh-VITCH") suddenly appears on scene to challenge a referee's ruling that a tennis ball went out of bounds. That song with this title is by Martin Solveig and Dragonette, who sings that she "just came to say" the title word. This word is followed by the question "is it me you are looking for" in a song by Lionel Richie. In a different song with this title, the singer notes that she has been "wondering if after all these years you'd like to meet" and claims she "must have called a thousand times." For 10 points, give the title word of the 2015 Adele song in which she says it "from the other side."

The complete description of this quantum mechanical system includes a term proportional to a Dirac delata function of position called the Darwin term. The angular portions of the wave functions that describe this system are proportional to terms given by the Rodrigues relation, the Laguerre polynomials, and a radiative correction known as the Lamb shift was discovered in this system. The spin-flip transition corresponding to 1420 megahertz in this quantum mechanical system is widely used in radio astronomy, arises from hyperfine splitting, and is called the 21-centimeter line, while another transition in this system that is useful in astronomy gives rise to the Lyman-alpha forest. With transition energies given by the Rydberg formula with Z equal to 1, for ten points, identify this system that also exhibits the Balmer and Paschen series and consists of a single electron bound to a single proton.

The preface to the poem states that the poet drew inspiration from Purchas his Pilgrimage and describes the poem as a "psychological curiosity". Places mentioned include "forests ancient as the hills" and "that deep romantic chasm", the source of a spring which bursts forth sending "huge fragments vaulted like rebounding hail". Later the poet describes a dulcimer being played by an "Abyssynian maid", and "voices prophesying war", and in it "a sunless sea" is approached by "Alph, the sacred river". For 10 points, name this poem in which "a stately pleasure dome" is decreed in Xanadu by the titular Mongol ruler, a poem by Samuel Taylor Coleridge.

this structure is essential for intestinal enzymes. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this duodenum-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The duodenum is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in intestinal enzymes.

parts.text: Name this author, one of whose poems is addressed from Catarina to a lover who has gone abroad. Another of this author's poems bids: "Gather the north flowers to complete the south."
The 43rd poem from Elizabeth Browning's Sonnets from the Portuguese begins by asking "how do I love thee?" before this five-word statement.
acceptableAnswers: The Let me count the ways

parts.text: Most of Elizabeth Browning's love poems are to Robert, but she did write a poem about "desire" for this person, describing her as a "large-brained woman and large-hearted man." In a poem titled for "recognition" of this person, Browning writes: "Beat purer, heart, and higher / Till God unsex thee on the heavenly shore."
acceptableAnswers: Amantine Lucile Aurore Dupin de Francueil

Gaddafi led this North African country, which disputed the Aouzou Strip with its southern neighbor, Chad. The U.S. embassy in this country's city of Benghazi was attacked in 2012.
The Aouzou strip is rich in deposits of this element, which can be processed from yellowcake. This element's 235 isotope is used in nuclear reactors.

parts.text: Give this two word term that describes the value lost in a trade-off by choosing to spend resources on a different option.
Opportunity cost is often described in economics by the food-related catchphrase that "there is no such thing as" one of these.

Someone who does receive a lunch at no cost is said to be a "free rider," benefiting from someone else's paying of the cost of the lunch. This "tragedy" is a scenario where free lunches, or other public goods, are exploited by individuals who don't replenish whatever resource is providing them.

bonuses.leadin: This economic concept can be illustrated by spending a Saturday playing quizbowl, as that's one fewer day you could spend doing homework, working a part-time job, or relaxing with friends. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this long-term characteristic of places that encompasses properties like temperature, atmospheric pressure, wind, and rainfall. Change in this characteristic may happen via global warming.
Climate is paired with considerations of animal life, plant life, and soil conditions to define these broad ecosystems, some of which include tundra, taiga, and savanna.

This climate classification system has six main divisions, labeled A through H. Various subtypes of climates are represented by two- to four-letter symbols in this system, named for a German climatologist.

bonuses.leadin: The study of these systems involves observation of patterns like the Northern Pacific Index and the Southern Oscillation. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This dating method is used to determine the order of past events by comparing the age of one object to an object of known age. The study of the order of the layer of rocks, stratigraphy, is a form of this dating method.
Radiometric dating, which is a form of absolute dating, uses this property of radioisotopes, which is the amount of time needed for the isotope's radioactivity to decay fifty percent.

One form of radiometric dating measures the decay of this element's radioactive isotope 40 into a stable argon atom, with a half-life of 1.25 billion years. This element is found in a namesake type of pink feldspar.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these dating methods that scientists use to establish the age of objects:

parts.text: Name this Ancient Greek dramatist, who also described the city of Cloudcuckooland in The Birds.

This first prize-winning Aristophanes work sees Dionysus travel to Hades to recover Euripides [yew-RIH-pih-deez], the "greatest Athenian tragedian." The title characters of this play are a chorus that chants "Brekekekex-koax-koax."

After a debate, this author of The Persians, Seven Against Thebes, and the Oresteia [ohr-eh-STY-uh] trilogy is brought back instead of Euripides. Adding insult to injury, this man suggests that Sophocles take his place as Hades' best tragic poet while he's away.

bonuses.leadin: Lampito and Myrrhine ["mere"-een] agree to Lysistrata's [liss-iss-trah-tah ‟s] scheme to end the Peloponnesian War in one of this man's plays. For 10 points each,

Stuart helps protect this character from Snowbell; by the end of the book, Stuart has set off to find her.

parts.text: Name this field of economics that focuses on conflict and cooperation. It is often represented by the prisoner's dilemma.

In the prisoner's dilemma, there is only one of these points, which is reached when both prisoners defect. These points are reached when neither player can improve their position with unilateral changes to strategy.
Game theory is often applied to these markets that often have kinked demand curves. These market's durability was demonstrated by Hotelling's linear city model.

This other major government program is funded by both the federal government and states. Its primary purpose is to insure people in poverty.

Due to gravity, a launched projectile travels in the path of this U-shaped figure. All quadratic functions form this shape when graphed.

This large lake surrounded by the Sahara desert is surprisingly shallow, only 34 feet deep at its lowest point. It is named after a country whose capital is N'Djamena.
This longest and second deepest lake in the world is located between Tanzania and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

parts.text: Name this effect in which reactions with different forms of the same element have different rates. This effect is most pronounced when replacing hydrogen with the significantly more massive deuterium.

The concentration dependence of the kinetic isotope effect can distinguish between SN1 [S-N-"one"] and SN2 [S-N-"two"] mechanisms by determining which of these short-lived entities forms as an intermediate during a reaction.

Theta-sub-nu, a constant with these units, can be used in place of the vibrational frequency to simplify the formula for the change in rate due to the kinetic isotope effect. That substitution is also used in the partition function to reduce the Boltzmann factor's exponent to a ratio of terms with these units.
acceptableAnswers: Celsius with “What exact units would be used?”

"A Scandal in Bohemia" also references this early Holmes novel, whose first half ends with Holmes arresting the man who murdered Enoch Drebber and Joseph Stangerson. Its second half is set primarily in Utah.
